checks.summary: All 24 values the model relied on match the filed statements. The model still marks Datadog's evidence as conflicting, because one of its own checks misreads how the company computes diluted earnings per share.
findings: The model's run records a failed check on fiscal 2025 diluted earnings per share. The check divides net income of $107.7 million by diluted shares and gets $0.30, against the filed $0.31. Datadog has convertible notes, and the filed calculation adds $3.7 million of note interest after tax back to the numerator, which gives $0.31. The filing is right and the check is wrong.
Stock compensation of $823.0 million is 67% of operating cash flow and 20.7% of revenue for the year to June 30, 2026.

The model's free cash flow leaves out $109.3 million of capitalized software development costs. With them, free cash flow is $1,072.8 million and the margin is 27.0% and not 29.8%. That lower figure matches the free cash flow measure the company publishes.
Operating income for the year to June 30, 2026, is $16.3 million, a margin of 0.4%. Other income of $183.5 million, most of it interest on cash, exceeds net income of $177.6 million.
Accounts payable added $106.1 million to operating cash flow in the latest period. The latest quarterly report ties the rise to the timing of cloud hosting invoices.
The latest quarterly report says the largest customer reduced its usage from the third quarter of 2026, which may slow revenue growth.
The annual change in share count of 3.3% is measured on basic shares. Fiscal 2022 was a loss year, so its diluted count equals its basic count.
review_corrections: The first check said no period lost shares to anti-dilution. No quarter had a net loss, but the filings exclude anti-dilutive awards in every period, 4.6 million shares in the first half of 2025.
The second reviewer could not confirm which of the model's checks failed, because it did not have the model's run records. The project read that record separately on the machine that holds the run.

The first check said no acquisition report had been filed since the middle of 2025 and that the April 2026 move to Nevada exchanged shares one for one. Neither statement rests on a document that was read, and both are unverified.
Filed diluted share averages are not additive across quarters, so the twelve-month diluted share rows reproduce the model's construction and do not establish the true figure.
review_additions: A 2025 tax law lowered income tax expense from the third quarter of 2025. The tax rate that quarter was about 5%. The filings do not give the amount of the benefit.
Datadog bought three companies in the first half of 2026 for $191.5 million and three in 2025 for $178.4 million. The company called them not material and gave no acquired revenue figure.
Currency movements account for $11.3 million of the rise in other income in the first half of 2026, while interest income fell slightly.

checks.summary: All 24 values the model relied on match the filed statements. The model failed to build one further value, cash spent on acquisitions, and so left its check for a change in business scope unevaluated.
findings: The model built no figure for cash spent on acquisitions. The filings give $173.1 million for the year to June 28, 2026, which is 5.9% of total assets. Year-to-date payments fell from $1.9 million to $1.7 million between the first and second quarters because of purchase price adjustments, and the model rejects a cumulative payment that shrinks.

About 4.9 of the 17.1 percentage points of revenue growth came from acquired businesses, and about 1.7 points came from currency. Organic growth was about 10.6 points. Five acquisitions closed in 2025, three of them in the fourth quarter.

Operating margin rose 1.4 percentage points, from 17.7% to 19.1%. Restructuring charges fell from $26.4 million to $8.8 million between the two periods, and without them the margin rose about 0.6 points. Gross margin fell in the first half of 2026.

Free cash flow rose $32.5 million while working capital used $119.1 million. Deferred income taxes swung by $60.9 million in the company's favor, and the latest quarterly report says the cash tax benefit from accelerated deductions will not repeat in 2026.
Neither period contains discontinued operations, a 53-week year or a restated comparative. No acquisition was reported after the latest balance sheet as of Sept. 18, 2026.
review_corrections: The first check overstated the rounding uncertainty in the annual change in share count. Share counts are filed to the nearest 0.1 million, so the range is about minus 0.2% to zero a year.
The first check said prior-year figures were unchanged in the later filing. One cash flow line was split into two in the later filing, with the same total.
The second reviewer could not confirm why the model rejected the acquisitions figure, because it did not have the model's code. The project confirmed that cause separately in the code.
review_additions: The earlier period includes a $7.8 million pension settlement gain before tax.
The later period includes a $3.4 million benefit from the release of a reserved contingency.
Acquisition-related charges after tax were $5.9 million in the later period and $3.7 million in the earlier one.

checks.summary: All 24 values the model relied on match the filed statements. Net income for the year to July 31, 2026, is mostly a one-time tax benefit, and the diluted share count a year earlier is 0.20% too low.
findings: Net income of $361.9 million for the year to July 31, 2026, exceeds income before tax of $210.9 million. UiPath released a $204.9 million valuation allowance on its United States deferred tax assets during fiscal 2026. Without the release, net income is about $157 million, and about 0.38 of the 0.52 diluted earnings per share for fiscal 2026 comes from it.

The model's diluted share count for the year to July 31, 2025, is 548.3 million, and the published quarterly counts average 549.4 million. Fiscal 2025 was a loss year, so its diluted count equals its basic count, and the model derives a profitable fourth quarter from it. The quarterly figure comes from the company's earnings release, which is furnished to the regulator and is not audited.
The annual change in share count of minus 0.6% is measured on basic shares. Measured on the diluted counts that the model displays beside it, the change is minus 0.2% a year.
Stock compensation fell from $329.5 million to $234.6 million between the two periods. That $94.9 million is about 48% of the $199.3 million improvement in operating income.

UiPath bought WorkFusion on Feb. 5, 2026, for $189.5 million, of which $160.0 million was cash, and paid $149.4 million net of cash acquired. It bought Peak AI for $38.1 million in the earlier period. The filings give no acquired revenue figure.
Deferred tax assets are $230.1 million of total assets on July 31, 2026, against $26.0 million a year earlier.
UiPath repurchased 22.8 million shares for $268.5 million in the first half of fiscal 2027 and 30.2 million shares for $329.1 million a year earlier.
review_corrections: The first check said the tax benefit inflates the price to earnings ratio. It inflates earnings, so it lowers that ratio; without the release the ratio is about 3.6 times higher at the same price.
The rise in deferred tax assets is not all the valuation allowance release. The WorkFusion purchase brought a separate deferred tax asset of $30.4 million.

The first check cited a report filed in September 2026 for a planned share conversion and said no acquisition had been reported after the balance sheet date. That report was not among the saved documents, so both statements are unverified.
The first check said the periods hold no investment gains and no discontinued operations. The statements show none, but the review did not establish that across every disclosure.
review_additions: The earlier period also holds a tax release, $24.7 million for the United Kingdom entity. Without it, the earlier period's net income of $20.2 million becomes a loss of about $4.5 million.
Restructuring expense fell from $16.5 million to $5.0 million between the two periods, which is about 6% of the improvement in operating income.
Other income in the first half of fiscal 2027 rose on $16.1 million more of currency gains and $7.1 million less of legal expense for shareholder litigation.
The acquisitions add expense as well as assets. Amortization of acquired intangibles was $10.6 million in the first half of fiscal 2027 against $3.7 million a year earlier.

checks.summary: Of the 24 values the model relied on, 23 match the filed statements. The diluted share count for the year to July 3, 2026, is 0.58% too low.
findings: The model's diluted share count for the year to July 3, 2026, is 76.79 million, and the published quarterly counts average 77.23 million. Fiscal 2025 and its first nine months were both loss periods, so their diluted counts equal their basic counts. The model derives the fourth quarter from those two figures and therefore uses a basic count for a quarter that earned $45.1 million. The quarterly figure comes from the company's earnings release, which is furnished to the regulator and is not audited.

Net income of $240.9 million for the year to July 3, 2026, exceeds operating income of $210.8 million. It includes a $41.5 million net fair value gain on the company's investment in IQE and a $10.1 million gain on acquired assets.

Net income a year earlier was a loss of $69.9 million on operating income of $117.6 million, because of a $193.1 million loss on the exchange of convertible notes in the quarter that ended Jan. 3, 2025.

Fiscal 2025 had 53 weeks, so the earlier period covers 371 days and the later one covers 364. Revenue grew 28.4% as reported and 30.8% after scaling the earlier period to 364 days, which is the adjustment the model applies.

Capital spending rose from $27.5 million to $67.1 million. That line excludes a $28.8 million property purchase under a financing arrangement in the earlier period, which an equal financing inflow offset, and it excludes $9.9 million of software license purchases in the later period.
Neither period contains a restated comparative. No acquisition was reported after the latest balance sheet as of Sept. 18, 2026.
review_corrections: The first check called the IQE holding one equity stake. It is $40.4 million of equity and $20.2 million of convertible debt, which produced a gain of about $49.6 million and a loss of about $8.1 million. These fair value changes will keep passing through earnings, so they are not a single event.
The first check cited a share issuance from fiscal 2026 to explain share growth that ended in fiscal 2025. The relevant issuance was 1,582,958 shares in December 2024.
The first check said there was no release of a tax valuation allowance. The second reviewer accepts only that the filings it read identify none.
review_additions: Fiscal 2025 includes a $10.1 million charge from a change in the tax valuation allowance, of which about $9.2 million relates to foreign losses the company does not expect to use.
Stock compensation was $83.6 million in the later period and is added back in operating cash flow.
The 2029 convertible notes carry $344.3 million of principal that must be settled in cash, and they are now classified as short-term debt.

checks.summary: Of the 24 values the model relied on, 22 match the filed statements. Revenue is wrong in both twelve-month periods, by 2.8% in the year to July 31, 2026, and by 2.4% a year earlier.
findings: The filed net revenues are $7,391 million for the year to July 31, 2026, and the model used $7,185 million. A year earlier the filed figure is $6,590 million and the model used $6,429 million. Since its fiscal 2026 annual report, NetApp labels the revenue of its Hybrid Cloud segment with the general revenue tag, and the model prefers that tag to the one that carries total net revenues. The gaps of $206 million and $161 million equal Public Cloud revenue.
Every ratio built on revenue moves with it. Operating margin is 25.0% and not 25.7%, the margin gain is 4.3 percentage points and not 4.5, and free cash flow margin is 22.3% and not 23.0%.

Fiscal 2027 has 53 weeks, and the extra week fell in the quarter that ended July 31, 2026. The company puts the extra week at about $65 million of services revenue and about $22 million of operating expense.

The model built no figure for cash spent on acquisitions. The filings give $78 million for the year to July 31, 2026, which is 0.7% of total assets. NetApp bought DataPelago on July 16, 2026, for $193 million, of which $87 million was paid in cash at closing and $106 million depends on future results.
NetApp sold its Spot business on March 3, 2025, inside the earlier period, and recorded no material gain or loss. Restructuring charges were about 1% of revenue in both periods.
Interest expense rose from $64 million to $109 million in fiscal 2026. No comparative figure was restated, and no acquisition was reported after the latest balance sheet as of Sept. 18, 2026.
review_corrections: The first check said the earlier annual report had no acquisitions line. It has one, and it shows zero for fiscal 2025, so the earlier figure is a filed zero.

The $65 million is only the services revenue that the company attributes to the extra week. The filing gives no figure for the whole effect, so a growth rate adjusted by $65 million is a partial adjustment.
The rise in goodwill over the year should not all be attributed to DataPelago. The purchase added $151 million, and currency translation accounts for part of the rest.

The second reviewer could not confirm why the model built no acquisitions figure or why it prefers the general revenue tag, because it did not have the model's code. The project confirmed both causes separately in the code.
review_additions: The earlier period includes a $36 million tax benefit from the release of tax reserves after an examination by the tax authority. Without it, net income grew about 25% and not 21%.
The later period includes a final transition tax payment of $179 million, which lowers operating cash flow and free cash flow for that period.
The sale of Spot removed revenue and amortization from the later period, and the Public Cloud gross margin rose nine percentage points. The two periods do not describe the same business scope.
The company called DataPelago's effect on its results not material.
The second reviewer could not open two reports filed in September 2026, because the first check had not saved them.
